articles.title: ‘Billy’s cesspool’ – Texas A&M Head calls out fan site, asks ‘real fans’ to stay behind the team
articles.summary: Aggies head coach Mike Elko has called out TexAgs owner Billy Liucci and fans online after Texas A&M’s latest disappointing loss led to intense online backla...
articles.body:
Aggies head coach Mike Elko has called out TexAgs owner Billy Liucci and fans online after Texas A&M's latest disappointing loss led to intense online backlash.

Texas A&M entered the season with high expectations under Mike Elko, but a 27-6 loss to Missouri dropped the Aggies to 3-3. The defeat followed an earlier loss to Kentucky, with the team's struggles on the field leading to a lot of frustration within the fanbase.

TexAgs, co-owned by Billy Liucci, is one of the biggest platforms covering the program. It has been one of the sites where criticism of Elko and the team has been the loudest. Elko's handling of the team's struggles has led to a lot of questions on the discussion hub, and he has now hit back at his critics.

Mike Elko says he 'doesn't care much' about online fans on TexAgs, calls it 'Billy's cesspool'

The landscape of sports fandom is constantly changing, and the modern era has brought its own peculiarities. Coaches and players now have to regularly deal with fans online pointing out their every failing and discussing every issue they have.

While it can be a lot to deal with sometimes, pushing back doesn't always help. Elko clearly doesn't agree, though, because he didn't mince words when calling out the fans on TexAgs.

"There's a difference to me between the fan base and social media," the coach said during his press conference. "So there's one group that I really don't care much about. Billy's cesspool (at TexAgs) can go be Billy's cesspool.

"Our fan base, stay with us, be behind us. We're going to build something that we told you we were going to build. So we're in a really bad spot right now, but we'll work our way out of it."

This isn't going to go over well with fans when the team is already underachieving. Speaking from a position of success can sometimes allow players or coaches to get away with it. For Elko, though, this will likely amplify the criticism and give his doubters more reasons to call him out if results don't improve.

articles.title: “Sam Leavitt Is a Turnover Machine”: CFB Champ & Ex-NFLer Rips LSU QB After Dramatic Loss to Kentucky
articles.summary: Sam Leavitt was supposed to give LSU a steady hand at quarterback. Instead, after that heartbreaker against Kentucky, a former national champion and former N...
articles.body:
Sam Leavitt was supposed to give LSU a steady hand at quarterback. Instead, after that heartbreaker against Kentucky, a former national champion and former NFL player is openly questioning whether he can hold on to the football. It's a harsh take, but it's landing at a bad moment.

"The real LSU I know when I came to LSU was some m—-s who line up, punch you in the mouth, win a game, get off the bus, and go home," Breiden Fehoko, who was part of LSU's 2019 Natty-winning team, said in an X post video . "But we can't even do that. Four and two, and Sam Levitt is a turnover machine, and I've been telling y'all that. I said he was gonna cost us the season just a week ago, and y'all had the nerve to say, 'Man, y'all keep giving this dude attention.' And look where we at right now. Four and two, still gotta play Texas, Bama, Mississippi State. Can't stand y'all, bro."

The defeat against Kentucky leaves LSU at 4-2 overall and 1-2 in SEC play. Sam Leavitt put up 275 yards, one interception and two touchdowns on 25-of-34 passing against Kentucky, a stat line plenty of quarterbacks would gladly take. LSU still lost 35-34 in overtime on October 10, 2026, and the finger-pointing started almost right away.

Leavitt also fumbled the ball once. Turnovers have been an issue for the quarterback, who was once a top prospect in the transfer portal when LSU secured him.

This wasn't a sudden outburst, either. Fehoko had already posted asking for a change at the position.

"I'm telling you LSU is going to win this game cause Kentucky is a bad team but for the love of god PLEASE GET SAM LEAVITT OFF THIS STARTING LINEUP MAN!" Fehoko posted on X.

That came after a week of publicly pushing for Landen Clark to get a bigger chance. Fehoko had called Clark "the answer" for the Tigers going forward and even suggested that life without Leavitt might help LSU.

The numbers from Leavitt's last five games explain some of the frustration. LSU went 4-1 in that stretch, with the only loss coming 24-32 at Ole Miss. He threw for 1,221 yards and 8 touchdowns, and ran for 220 yards and 6 more scores. But he also tossed 7 interceptions, including three against Louisiana Tech. The one against Kentucky seems to be adding to a continuous tally.

"Don't ever let anything like that into my next play in the game," Leavitt said after the game, addressing the issue. "Gotta be strong mentality. That's all."

"Yeah, a lot of good (in Leavitt's performance). And obviously the turnover, bad," head coach Lane Kiffin said. "And myself, with the field goal, with the guy open for a touchdown, but I thought outside of that he played really good. He made a lot of good plays in the game."

Next up, the Tigers try to bounce back at home against Mississippi State.

articles.title: Physicality wasn't the problem for Alabama football defense vs Georgia
articles.summary: Physicality was never a question for Alabama football's defensive performance against Georgia.
articles.body:
When asked about Alabama football's defensive performance in its 20-17 loss to Georgia on Saturday, Oct. 10, coach Kalen DeBoer talked about Gunner Stockton .

The Georgia quarterback was clutch, DeBoer said. Stockton was in control and efficient. Combining that with a Bulldogs run game that had 206 rushing yards and averaged 5.3 yards per carry, "it's tough to stop."

Alabama forced four fumbles, none of which were secured by the Crimson Tide defense. The Crimson Tide had a Bray Hubbard interception and another by QB Reese that was later overturned by the officiating crew.

"You make your own breaks," DeBoer said. "You make your own breaks."

But it's not that Alabama played poorly defensively. Alabama allowed 455 yards and 20 points to the top scoring offense in the country. The approach was the same too, using turnovers and attempted pressure to try and beat the Bulldogs.

Alabama defensive back Keon Sabb saw a unit that didn't live up to "the standard" on its opportunities to get off the field, whether it be on third down or "bang-bang plays."

But neither he nor defensive back Bray Hubbard doubted Alabama's "physicality."

"Physicality was there," Sabb said. "They made plays, we made plays. But our physicality was there for sure."

"We played physical all night," Hubbard added. "I'm not going to ever say we didn't play physical, because that's a physical team. We matched their physicality and brought it to a higher level."

Alabama hustled. Alabama gave "everything" against Georgia. The effort was there.

"There's just some execution errors or just us being a step slow or just short of getting the football," DeBoer said. "That's the difference in the game."

articles.title: Cardiff lacked aggression in Rovers loss, says boss
articles.summary: Brian Barry-Murphy says his Cardiff side can have no excuses and were not good enough during their 2-1 defeat at Blackburn Rovers.
articles.body:
Brian Barry-Murphy says his Cardiff side lacked an aggressive edge as they were ultimately "not good enough" during their 2-1 defeat at Blackburn Rovers.

The Cardiff boss was left thoroughly disappointed, and noted their much-improved second-half performance only deepened his frustrations.

Cardiff were two down at the break after Andri Gudjohnsen closed down Joel Bagan's clearance to score and Todd Cantwell swept home after an incisive Rovers counter.

And though Calum Robinson pulled one back to give the travelling Bluebirds fans hope, Cardiff head home with nothing to show for their efforts and remain on one win.

"I'm very disappointed with our performance. We didn't feel as though it was good enough to give ourselves a chance to win the game," said head coach Barry-Murphy.

"We showed signs of what we are capable of in the second half, which probably only heightens our disappointment with how we played in the first half.

"We created good chances in the second half and should have scored a second. We can't shy away from the fact that we weren't good enough in the first half."

After that disappointing opening 45 minutes at Ewood Park, Barry Murphy felt his side created good chances in the second half and should have scored a second goal.

Overall, however, he accepted his side fell short.

"We knew how tough the challenge was going to be today. We gave the ball away in really dangerous areas.

"By our standards, we weren't good enough in possession. We lacked aggressiveness. We stepped back today and didn't push forward. That cost us."

Cardiff got themselves back into the game soon after the restart when Robinson drilled into the bottom corner to open his account for the season.

Fellow Republic of Ireland international Jack Moylan went close to scoring two fine solo goals, but the Bluebirds lacked the clinical edge to find an equaliser.

"We had really good situations, and with the players we have, we would back ourselves to find the correct solutions," said Barry-Murphy.

"We pushed right until the end, I've got no qualms about that, but I do not want to shy away or make excuses.

"We have to be really clear and honest with ourselves that we were not good enough today. We have to take it on the chin."

Cardiff will get the chance to put things right when they host fellow Championship strugglers Watford on Tuesday, 13 October (19:45 BST).

articles.title: MVDs: Alabama Edition
articles.summary: You don’t stride onto Nick Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium and take down the Crimson Tide without a total team effort. Still, even in a heroic victory li...
articles.body:
You don't stride onto Nick Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium and take down the Crimson Tide without a total team effort. Still, even in a heroic victory like this one some Georgia Bulldogs are bound to distinguish themselves over and above their teammates. Those dauntless ''Dawgs are your MVDs, the most valuable Dawgs from Georgia's 20-17 win over the Alabama Crimson Tide.

Offense. Everyone.Literally everyone. Gunner Stockton. Dwight Phillips, The whole dang offensive line. The ten different receivers who caught passes. Mike Bobo, who called arguably the best game he has in years. There's just no way to pick a single person for this honor. It was indeed a gutsy team effort.

Defense: Chris Cole. On any given Saturday Chris Cole is all over the football field, but on this evening "the Tarantula" was even more omnipresent than usual. Cole notched 8 total tackles, 5 of them solo stops. He had 2.5 tackles for loss, and broke up 2 passes in coverage. He also affected Keelon Russell on several occasions that don't show up on the stat sheet but were nevertheless indispensable to victory. Big time players make big time plays in big games. And Chris Cole had himself a by golly big game in this big game.

Special teams: Peyton Woodring. For the first time in awhile the Bulldog punt return game felt like a liability rather than an asset. Drew Miller's two punts were a 52 yarder into the endzone that should have been a 45 yarder inside the ten, and a 40 yard clunker that gave the Tide the ball at midfield. In the land of the blind the man who hits one field goal is king. Woodring shrugged off his first missed field goal of the season to come back and hit the23 yarder that turned out to be the game winner. That kind of mental fortitude is critical for a kicker, and we are absolutely spoiled at the position with Woodring.

Incidentally, Woodring also produced touchbacks on 4 of 5 kickoffs, with the other being returned from the endzone zone to the 34 but backed up to the 11 thanks to a Bama penalty. That's pretty dang good by itself on a wet, windy night in a hostile stadium, and shouldn't be overlooked.

articles.title: Will Shohei Ohtani decide Dodgers' fate in NLCS?
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani and the Los Angeles Dodgers are back in the National League Championship Series for a third consecutive season.
articles.body:
Shohei Ohtani and the Los Angeles Dodgers are back in the National League Championship Series for a third consecutive season.

The Dodgers will be tasked with beating the Milwaukee Brewers , who produced the best record in the league this season. This is the second consecutive season the two teams have met in the NLCS.

Los Angeles managed to sweep Milwaukee in 2025, holding the Brewers' offense to just one run in each game. Ohtani was named the series MVP, having delivered a strong two-way performance.

The Dodgers' superstar closed out last year's NLCS by pitching six shutout innings while striking out 10. He also hit three home runs in the game.

MLB teams ranked by their World Series championships

Will Shohei Ohtani need another strong performance for Dodgers to win?

Ohtani has not been healthy for a good portion of the 2026 season.

He was limited as a pitcher, and hasn't pitched at all since July 3 due to his injuries. It is unlikely that he will pitch during the postseason.

Ohtani will remain available as a designated hitter, despite dealing with knee inflammation and biceps discomfort.

The lack of pitching from Ohtani will not diminish Los Angeles' chances of making the World Series. Ohtani did not pitch during his first season with the Dodgers in 2024, but the team captured the World Series title anyway.

He spent the entire 2024 season recovering from right elbow surgery he underwent in September 2023. The four-time MVP reached several career milestones that year and created the 50-50 club after producing 54 home runs and 59 stolen bases.

Ohtani produced just two hits and a run in four games against the Atlanta Braves in the 2026 National League Division Series. He did not hit a home run but did steal a base. He was walked twice and struck out four times.

articles.title: Penn State football's pass rush problem spelled doom in loss to USC
articles.summary: The Nittany Lions' pass rush defense failed in all measures to contain USC and consigned it to a third straight loss to open Big Ten play.
articles.body:
STATE COLLEGE − Penn State football has a pass rush problem, and nowhere was it more evident than in its 31-23 loss to USC.

In front of the biggest recorded crowd in Beaver Stadium − 114,419 announced − the Nittany Lions defense was picked apart by USC quarterback Jayden Maiava. All night long, the Lions struggled to contain or pressure the senior quarterback as he took his time racking up 301 yards and three touchdowns on 21-for-33 passing.

For a time, the Lions seemed to mitigate, albeit not fully contain Maiava. He completed four of his last 10 pass attempts before halftime for 90 yards. But USC adjusted, and Penn State stuck to a three-man rush that failed to contain Maiava and let a flock of Trojan receivers run rampant to spoil the White Out game for the second year in a row.

"We tried to have some multiplicity in terms of what we were doing, especially for the quarterback," head coach Matt Campbell said. "Some of the biggest killers were some of the third down opportunities that we weren't able to finish on. The 3rd-and-10, 3rd-and-12, 3rd-and-13 opportunities, getting them to those points and not finishing − those were the biggest killers."

USC went 5-for-11 on third down conversions Saturday night. All five successful conversions came off a pass by Maiava, including the 10-yard touchdown pass in the fourth quarter that put the put the game out of reach for Penn State. Maiava was sacked once by Tony Rojas in the first quarter, and the defensive line only hurried him a single time all game.

It's not that Penn State's pass rush was bad against USC. It was nonexistent. The Lions couldn't shut down the Trojans ' passing game, which put pressure on their own offense to pick up the slack. An offense which still didn't have a definitive rushing identity Saturday and struggled to convert on third down. And when the three-man rush didn't work, the Lions refused to change up their gameplan and stuck to the same routine that let Maiava run wild in the pocket.

"We all just need to continue to get better," defensive end Yvan Kemajou, who recorded the Lions' only quarterback hurry of the game, said. "We've got to be more detailed. We've got to make sure we know what we're doing, that we're tackling and finishing."

Kemajou doesn't believe it's a conditioning problem. Neither does Campbell. Maybe so, but the Lions are far from where they need to be to stack up defensively while being three games deep into their Big Ten schedule. Campbell remains frustrated that the pieces haven't fit together yet, even as the Lions have wrapped the first half of their season. Three losses to open Big Ten play, no matter the score, speak volumes.

Jack Gleckler covers high school sports and Penn State football. Reach him at JGleckler@nncogannett.com.

articles.title: 3 takeaways from Utah’s home win over Kansas
articles.summary: It wasn’t the prettiest of performances from the Utes, but they got the job done against a high-passing Kansas offense
articles.body:
Originally planned to start at 8:15 but moved up because of forecasted showers, the game between Utah and Kansas was a very odd one to say the least, but the Utes made enough big plays to emerge the victors, 41-24.

All momentum was Utah's until it wasn't in the last minute of the first half.

The Utes struck early and fast to go up 14-0 while the Jayhawks couldn't get anything to work on the offensive side of the ball. Their only touchdown in the first 28-plus minutes came off David Santiago's strip of Devon Dampier inside Utah's 10.

But Utah also struggled to come by points after the initial two drives other than when Kansas helped out with a slew of penalties, and in the final 1:09 before halftime, the Jayhawks scored 10 points as quarterback Isaiah Marshall was able to penetrate the Utah secondary through the air and got to do it again when Kansas' defense picked Dampier off near midfield, resulting in three points before the half.

But the Utes weathered the storm and got enough big plays from their defense, including a massive fourth down stop inside their own 1 yard line to suck the life out of the Jayhawks.

On Utah's third scoring drive of the game, Dampier tossed two underthrown balls that actually ended up benefiting the Utes as the receivers were run into as they tried to come back to the ball.

Had the first pass interference not occurred, it would have stalled Utah's drive. Instead, the Utes extended it twice as the Kansas cornerbacks never turned around to locate the ball.

If the corners had been able to turn around, both passes might have easily been picked off.

But, instead, they resulted in plus yardage for the Utes as Kansas head coach Lance Leipold was penalized with unsportsmanlike conduct — which he later said was not anger directed at the the officials — to decrease Utah's distance to the goal all the more, ultimately resulting in a short reception thrown to Noah Bennee in the end zone.

While the underthrown passes ended up assisting the Utes' drive, the throws were uncharacteristic of Dampier, who is generally an accurate passer, though he may be revealing his difficulty throwing long distances.

A heave eventually came back to the bite the quarterback as the Jayhawks turned an interception with about 30 seconds left before halftime into three points.

Dampier did clean up the throws in the second half, but too many underthrown ones like the first half, and corners will be sure to get their heads to the ball.

Wayshawn Parker got five touches in the first quarter as the Utes saw a fair amount of success running the offense through the speedy back.

He only had three touches in the second quarter as Kansas started to creep back in it.

Part of that was due to the Jayhawks' ability to contain the run with their defensive ends, who made their presence known throughout the night.

However, Utah did end up calling Parker's number in the second half and he ended with 16 carries on the night for 171 yards, including an 89-yard score to pretty much seal the win for Utah shortly after a massive fourth-down stop at their own 1-yard line.

Moving forward, one thing has to be clear to Morgan Scalley and his staff, get the ball to Parker. It does not matter if it is a handoff, a pass, pitch or a direct snap — he'll make something happen.

Utah's defense struggled but came up big enough in the end

To begin the game, Utah only allowed one first down by the Jayhawks in the first half up until nearly the last minute, when Kansas finally found a groove against a Utah defense that has not seen as successful a passing attack as Marshall and Kansas' in quite some time.

Whether not enough pressure from the defensive line, or some breakdowns covering Cam Pickett, who recorded 134 receiving yards on 14 targets, Kansas may have exposed something more teams will look capitalize on.

But despite the struggles in the second half, the Ute defense held the Jayhawk rushing attack to under 60 yards on the night and came up big to get the red zone stops they needed to put the visitors away.

After an overturned touchdown that put Kansas inside the 1, Utah's pressure managed to stop Marshall from turning the corner for a turnover on downs, which set up Parker's second touchdown of the night.

The Jayhawks' next drive saw them get stopped again in the red zone despite having a fresh set of downs after a pass interference call.

It may not have been the prettiest of nights for the Ute defense, but they managed to get the job done when it mattered most.

articles.title: Penn State hockey can't complete comeback effort in tough road loss
articles.summary: Penn State's third period rally can't lift Nittany Lions to a win in Ice Breaker Tournament loss to Sacred Heart.
articles.body:
After climbing back from a three-goal deficit, Penn State hockey could not quite complete the comeback effort with a win on Saturday night. The Nittany Lions fell on the road against Sacred Heart, 6-3, to wrap up its first weekend of the season with back-to-back losses in the Ice Breaker Tournament in Connecticut.

Josh Fleming got the night off after protecting the goal Friday night in a loss at UConn . Ryder Fetterolf stood in goal for the Nittany Lions. Fetterolf made a couple of blocks on an odd-man rush by Sacred Heart but could not stop the third off a rebound as Sacred Heart struck first in the second period. A defensive turnover led to another Sacred Heart goal nearly midway through the second period as Fetterolf was unable to bail the Nittany Lions out of a jam. A fortunate bounce of the puck off the boards and an official led to a one-timer by Emmanuel Vermette to score a goal to put Sacred Heart up 3-0 late in the second period.

Penn State must have had an inspiring pep talk during the second intermission because Penn State came out swinging to start the third period. Kale Dach ignited a three-goal flurry in a span of 87 seconds as Penn State answered quickly at the start of the third period. Justin Larose scored his first goal of the season 21 seconds later and then captain Dane Dowiak tied the game at 3-3 a minute later.

Sacred Heart answered after things calmed down a bit with a goal midway through the period off the stick of Landen Gunderson, scoring his second goal of the game to give the Pioneers a 4-3 lead. A pair of empty-net goals padded the final box score as Penn State fell to 0-2-0 to start the season.

A night after outshooting UConn, Penn State was on the other end of things after being out-shot by Sacred Heart 40-25. Penn State was perfect on the penalty kill this weekend but failed to score on five power play opportunities against UConn and Sacred Heart. This was the first loss Penn State suffered against Sacred Heart in the seventh all-time meeting between the two clubs.

The Nittany Lions will face another tough non-conference challenge next weekend when it opens the doors to Pegula Ice Arena for the first time this season. Penn State will host No. 6 Quinnipiac for one game on Friday, Oct. 16. The game is scheduled to start at 7:00 p.m.
